2607.28609.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
2607.28609.paper_summary: Computer-using agents (CUAs) are advancing rapidly across the digital world. A CUA trajectory records the agent's actions, states, and reasoning. Verifying whether it fulfilled the task instruction is central to CUA evaluation, data curation, and reinforcement learning. Neither human-written verifiers nor human annotators can provide such verification at scale, so the field increasingly turns to vision-language models (VLMs) as judges of CUA trajectories. But a fundamental question has long gone unexamined: are these VLM judges reliable enough? To study it systematically, we introduce OSReward, a realistic, high-quality benchmark that evaluates VLM judges on CUA trajectories. The trajectories come from diverse agent backbones executing human-verified instructions across platforms, then rigorously labeled with ground-truth verdicts through multi-stage human annotation. Building on it, we derive OSReward-Hard, a challenge set concentrating genuinely hard cases, and OSReward-Multi for fine-grained efficiency and alignment scoring. The most comprehensive evaluation of VLM judges to date finds even state-of-the-art models fall short of an ideal judge, sharing a systematic leniency bias that mislabels failed runs as successes. The few reliable enough to trust are too expensive to run at scale, while affordable open models trail far behind. To close this gap, we construct and release OS-Shepherd-100K, an open corpus of reasoning-annotated trajectory judgments for the CUA community. On it, we train OS-Shepherd (9B and 35B), open reward models that supply low-cost, stable, and reliable reward signals, matching commercial judges at 30-60% lower cost than the frontier. Extensive analyses further inform the design of reliable CUA reward at scale. Our code, benchmark, dataset, and model checkpoints are available at https://os-copilot.github.io/OSReward-Home/.
2607.28609.paper_summary_zh: 電腦使用代理（CUAs）在數位世界中迅速發展。CUA 軌跡記錄了代理的行動、狀態和推理。驗證其是否完成任務指令是 CUA 評估、數據策展和強化學習的核心。人類撰寫的驗證者和人類標註者無法大規模提供這樣的驗證，因此該領域越來越多地轉向視覺語言模型（VLMs）作為 CUA 軌跡的評判者。但一個根本性問題長期未被檢視：這些 VLM 評判者是否足夠可靠？為了系統性地研究這一問題，我們介紹了 OSReward，一個現實的高品質基準，用於評估 VLM 評判者在 CUA 軌跡上的表現。這些軌跡來自於多樣的代理骨幹，執行跨平台的人類驗證指令，然後通過多階段的人類標註嚴格標記為真實判決。在此基礎上，我們推導出 OSReward-Hard，一個集中於真正困難案例的挑戰集，以及 OSReward-Multi，用於細緻的效率和對齊評分。迄今為止對 VLM 評判者的最全面評估發現，即使是最先進的模型也未達到理想評判者的標準，並且共享一種系統性的寬容偏見，將失敗的運行錯誤標記為成功。少數可靠到足以信任的模型運行成本過高，無法大規模使用，而可負擔的開放模型則遠遠落後。為了縮小這一差距，我們構建並發布了 OS-Shepherd-100K，這是一個為 CUA 社群提供推理標註的軌跡判決的開放語料庫。在此基礎上，我們訓練了 OS-Shepherd（9B 和 35B），開放獎勵模型，提供低成本、穩定且可靠的獎勵信號，其成本比商業評判者低 30-60%。廣泛的分析進一步為大規模可靠 CUA 獎勵的設計提供了信息。我們的代碼、基準、數據集和模型檢查點可在 https://os-copilot.github.io/OSReward-Home/ 獲得。
